newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels call Algerian poll "a farce".
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels call Algerian poll "a farce".

text.p: Moslem fundamentalist rebels said on Sunday Algeria's referendum on a new constitution had been rigged and farcical and was a threat to the credibility of future elections.
"The farce has taken place, as expected," said a statement from the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front's (FIS) leadership in exile, faxed to Reuters in Paris.
"As expected, the results announced did not comform to reality. Rigging and exaggeration are such that they deprive the operation of any credibility," it said.
According to official figures, 85.8 percent of voters in last week's poll backed President Liamine Zeroual's proposed constitution, which bans Islamic parties and strengthens the president's powers.

FIS said the population had been completely indifferent to the poll which it said "deprives the rulers from the credibility they were seeking and threatens the credibility of the polls they plan for the coming months".
It called on Zeroual to end repression and open serious political dialogue.
Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia said recently that government forces had won the battle against Moslem rebels and guerrillas' "residual terrorism" would be wiped out in the near future.
More than 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities annulled a general election in which FIS had taken a huge lead.
